chart.title: You — general statements
rows: What can you do on this computer?
You can play games and do homework.
How do you make vegetable soup?
First, you wash the vegetables. Then you cook them.
How do you use that invention?
You press the button and you turn the wheel.
chart.note: In English, 'you' can mean 'people in general' — not one specific person. It is used to give instructions or explain how things work. 'How do you use it?' means 'How does one use it?' or 'How do people use it?'

sentences: How do you use that toy?
You press the button to turn it on.
First, you put the battery inside.
You can find good ideas everywhere.
You turn the wheel and it moves.
You need creativity to invent things.
How do you solve this problem?
You lift the lid to open it.
You can succeed if you keep trying.

rules.title: 'You' for people in general
rules.explanation: In English, 'you' doesn't always mean one specific person. It can mean 'people in general' — like saying 'one' or 'people' in other languages.
examples: You need a battery to use this.
You can find good ideas everywhere.

rules.title: 'How do you...?' — asking about general process
rules.explanation: Use 'How do you + verb?' to ask how something works or how to do something in general. It is not asking one specific person.
examples: How do you use this invention?
How do you make the wheels turn?

rules.title: Giving instructions with 'you'
rules.explanation: Use 'you + verb' to give step-by-step instructions. This is common in recipes, manuals, and explanations.
examples: First, you put the battery in. Then you press the button.
You lift your arms and shake your legs.
